boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Auburn University
boards.description: Navigate Auburn after dark with these under-21-safe late-night destinations, from 24-hour campus markets and study halls to iconic off-campus diners and safe transit options.

cards.title: 24/7 Campus Provisions
cards.subtitle: Central Dining Commons
cards.notes: Access snacks, beverages, and microwaveable meals 24/7 using your Tiger Card at this automated market located near the ACLC.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 automated campus market providing essential snacks and meals for late-night study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Students may access and purchase food 24/7 at the Central Market located in the Central Dining Commons.
cards.source_title: Central Market - Auburn University Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for students with valid university identification.

cards.title: Safe Campus Transit
cards.subtitle: Campus-Wide Service
cards.notes: Request a safe ride between any two on-campus locations from 6 p.m. to 7 a.m. daily through the Auburn Safety app.
cards.short_summary: A university-operated shuttle service ensuring safe point-to-point travel across campus throughout the night.
cards.evidence_claim: The Night Security Shuttle operates between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m. and transports passengers to on-campus locations only.
cards.source_title: Night Security Shuttle Service | Campus Safety and Security
cards.access_notes: Available 6 p.m. to 7 a.m. daily for students and staff.

cards.title: The Midnight Study Hub
cards.subtitle: 231 Mell Street
cards.notes: Utilize extensive study spaces and collaborative zones; check the library website for current late-night and 24-hour finals schedules.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus library offering late-night study environments and resources for Auburn students.
cards.evidence_claim: Auburn University Libraries provide updated fall hours and study spots for the semester ahead.
cards.source_title: Auburn University Libraries - Facebook
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by semester; typically open until midnight or later during peak academic periods.

cards.title: Late-Night Tray Tradition
cards.subtitle: 333 S College St
cards.notes: Visit this popular drive-thru for signature trays and over 40 milkshake flavors, open until 3 a.m. or later.
cards.short_summary: A staple late-night fast-food destination known for its diverse menu and extended early-morning hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Cook Out locations typically close at 3:00 AM on weekdays and 4:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Cookout Hours 2026: Open, Close & Holiday Times
cards.access_notes: Open until 3 a.m. Sun-Thu and 4 a.m. Fri-Sat.

cards.title: 24-Hour Diner Classic
cards.subtitle: 2167 S College St
cards.notes: Enjoy classic diner fare any time of night at this 24-hour location situated south of the main campus.
cards.short_summary: A reliable 24-hour diner serving breakfast and comfort food to students at all hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Waffle House at 2167 S College St is open 24 hours daily for dine-in and takeout.
cards.source_title: Waffle House #1035 - Auburn, AL
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Late-Night Pizza Slices
cards.subtitle: 129 E Magnolia Ave
cards.notes: Grab a slice or a whole pie at this downtown favorite, open until 2 a.m. on weekdays and 3 a.m. on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A popular downtown pizzeria offering late-night service and Italian-style comfort food.
cards.evidence_claim: Little Italy Auburn is open Monday-Thursday until 2:00am and Friday-Saturday until 3:00am.
cards.source_title: Contact Us - Little Italy Auburn
cards.access_notes: Open until 2 a.m. Mon-Thu and 3 a.m. Fri-Sat.

cards.title: Always-Open Burger Run
cards.subtitle: 101 N College St
cards.notes: Located steps from Toomer's Corner, this 24-hour spot is a go-to for burgers and late-night breakfast.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour fast-food chain located in the heart of downtown Auburn near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Whataburger at 101 N College St offers 24-hour service and delivery in Auburn.
cards.source_title: Whataburger Auburn, AL | Burgers, Fast Food, Shakes
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: 24/7 Engineering Lab
cards.subtitle: Broun Hall, Room 123
cards.notes: Engineering students can access this computer lab 24/7 for late-night projects and technical work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated 24-hour computer lab for engineering students located in Broun Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Engineering computer labs, including Broun 123, are open 24 hours, 7 days a week while classes are in session.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs - Auburn Engineering
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access for engineering students; closed during home football weekends from Friday midnight to Sunday noon.

cards.title: Late-Night Slider Stop
cards.subtitle: 1927 S College St
cards.notes: Famous for its square burgers, this 24-hour location provides a quick late-night meal option south of campus.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour quick-service restaurant known for its signature sliders and late-night availability.
cards.evidence_claim: The Krystal at 1927 S. College Street in Auburn is open 24 hours daily.
cards.source_title: Auburn, AL | Krystal Restaurants
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: The Late-Night Living Room
cards.subtitle: 255 Heisman Drive
cards.notes: Gather for late-night study or socializing until 11 p.m. daily in the heart of campus.
cards.short_summary: A central campus hub offering study areas and resources until late evening.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harold D. Melton Student Center is open until 11 p.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Harold D. Melton Student Center - Auburn University Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open until 11 p.m. daily.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study nooks, quiet courtyards, and rooftop terraces that Auburn students use for daily productivity and relaxation beyond the standard landmark stops.

cards.title: The Deep Quiet Zone
cards.subtitle: Ralph Brown Draughon Library
cards.notes: Head to the top floor for strictly enforced individual quiet study. It is the campus standard for distraction-free finals prep.
cards.short_summary: The designated silent floor of Auburn's main library, preferred for intense individual focus.
cards.evidence_claim: The entire 4th floor of the Ralph Brown Draughon (RBD) Library is officially designated as a quiet study area.
cards.source_title: Are there any quiet study areas in the library? - LibAnswers
cards.access_notes: Open to students during library operating hours; Tiger Card required for late-night entry.

cards.title: Mell Street Collaboration Hub
cards.subtitle: Mell Classroom Building
cards.notes: Use the glass-enclosed 'collaboratories' for group projects. These rooms feature integrated tech and whiteboards for team sessions.
cards.short_summary: High-tech group study rooms located in the Mell Classroom Building adjacent to the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mell Classroom Building features 'collaboratories' and glass-enclosed study rooms designed for group work and interactive education.
cards.source_title: Auburn University Mell Classroom Building @ RBD Library - AIA Georgia
cards.access_notes: Rooms can be reserved by students via the Skedda system using an AU email.

cards.title: The 16-Acre Outdoor Classroom
cards.subtitle: Garden Drive
cards.notes: Walk the shaded trails to find quiet benches for reading. It is a primary spot for students to escape the noise of College Street.
cards.short_summary: A serene botanical garden on campus used by students for nature walks and quiet reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Davis Arboretum is a 16-acre botanic garden open daily from sunrise to sunset with no admission charge.
cards.source_title: Donald E. Davis Arboretum | College of Sciences and Mathematics
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; free and open to the public.

cards.title: Stadium View Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Horton-Hardgrave Hall
cards.notes: Visit the 4th-floor rooftop for covered outdoor seating and views of Jordan-Hare Stadium. It is a favorite for open-air studying.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop terrace in the business complex offering collaborative spaces and campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gavin Terrace on the 4th floor of Horton-Hardgrave Hall offers covered seating and views of Jordan-Hare Stadium.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students during building hours; features flexible and convertible spaces.

cards.title: The Campus Family Room
cards.subtitle: Heisman Drive
cards.notes: Utilize the upper-floor lounges for a mix of social and quiet space. The building also houses the Foy Information Desk for any campus questions.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, offering various lounges, dining, and meeting spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harold D. Melton Student Center provides 184,000 square feet of space for student meeting rooms, study areas, and lounges.
cards.source_title: AU Facilities Management - Melton Student Center Building Profile
cards.access_notes: Open daily; hours vary by semester but typically include late-night access.

cards.title: The Design School Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Dudley Hall
cards.notes: Relax in 'The Grove' section of the courtyard, which features moveable chairs and a shady canopy of trees near the architecture studios.
cards.short_summary: A renovated series of outdoor spaces including a theater forecourt and a shaded grove.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dudley Yards include 'The Grove,' a courtyard space with a shady grove of trees and moveable chairs.
cards.source_title: Dudley Yards - Auburn - HILLWORKS
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space accessible to all students.

cards.title: Artistic Study Escape
cards.subtitle: South College Street
cards.notes: Spread out on the museum grounds or use the lobby's modular couches for reading. The walking path is exactly one mile for three loops.
cards.short_summary: The university's fine art museum offering quiet indoor and outdoor spaces for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art offers free admission and grounds with landscaped walking paths and sculptures.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; Tiger Transit runs to this location on the South Quad-Fine Arts Line.

cards.title: The Business Hub
cards.subtitle: Lowder Hall Ground Floor
cards.notes: Find the student study area in room 023 on the ground floor. It is conveniently located near the building's Starbucks for quick breaks.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study area within the Harbert College of Business complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Lowder Hall's ground floor includes a designated student study area in room 023.
cards.source_title: Harbert College of Business Locations - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Open during business school operating hours; team rooms require reservation via Mazévo.

cards.title: Modern Lab Complex Nooks
cards.subtitle: Academic Classroom and Laboratory Complex
cards.notes: Look for the relaxation and quiet study areas tucked between the labs. This new facility offers some of the most modern furniture on campus.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study and relaxation zones within the new ACLC building near the campus amphitheater.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Classroom and Laboratory Complex (ACLC) features adaptable classroom spaces and quiet study areas.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Open to students during academic building hours.

cards.entity_name: Walt and Ginger Woltosz Rooftop Terrace
cards.title: The Culinary View
cards.subtitle: Tony and Libba Rane Culinary Science Center
cards.notes: Access this terrace before 3 p.m. for a quiet study spot with garden spaces and views of Samford Hall.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop garden terrace that serves as a student study spot during daytime hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The rooftop terrace at the Rane Culinary Science Center is open to students for study until 3 p.m. each day.
cards.source_title: Find out where students are studying this fall - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Open to students until 3:00 PM daily before transitioning to a commercial venue.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Auburn University, from world-class art galleries and botanical gardens to historic campus landmarks and nature preserves.

cards.entity_name: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
cards.title: Browse the Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: 901 South College Street
cards.notes: Visit this accredited museum for free to see 19th and 20th-century art. Enjoy the sculpture grounds and free coffee or tea during student social hours.
cards.short_summary: An accredited university art museum offering free admission to its galleries and landscaped sculpture grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art is free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: College Students - Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday 10:00 AM to 4:30 PM; extended hours until 8:00 PM on Thursdays.

cards.title: Walk the Native Plant Trails
cards.subtitle: 181 Garden Drive
cards.notes: Explore 16 acres of native Alabama plants and miles of walking trails. Look for the 170-year-old Founder's Oak near the center of the garden.
cards.short_summary: A 16-acre botanical garden and outdoor classroom featuring native Southeastern plants and walking trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Davis Arboretum is free and open to the public daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Donald E. Davis Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Parking is free on weekends and university holidays.

cards.title: Hike the Nature Trails
cards.subtitle: 2222 North College Street
cards.notes: Trek through 120 acres of forest with over six miles of trails. Visit the butterfly garden or the nature playground for a quiet escape from campus.
cards.short_summary: A 120-acre nature preserve offering miles of hiking trails, educational exhibits, and a nature playground.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kreher Preserve and Nature Center is free and open to the public 7 days a week from sunrise to sunset.
cards.source_title: Rules and Information - Kreher Preserve & Nature Center
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. No biking or pets allowed on the grounds.

cards.title: Lounge at Samford Park
cards.subtitle: 182 South College Street
cards.notes: Relax on the iconic lawn in front of Samford Hall. This central campus hub is the primary spot for student gatherings and outdoor study sessions.
cards.short_summary: The historic heart of Auburn's campus, featuring expansive green space for socializing and university traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford Lawn is a public campus space used for student life and traditions without admission fees.
cards.source_title: Samford Lawn - Auburn-Opelika Tourism
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space; buildings are typically locked on game days and holidays.

cards.title: Roll the Toomer's Oaks
cards.subtitle: College St & Magnolia Ave
cards.notes: Join the community tradition of rolling the trees with toilet paper after an Auburn victory. Participation is free and open to all fans.
cards.short_summary: A historic university tradition where fans celebrate victories by rolling the oaks at the campus entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition of rolling Toomer's Corner is a public celebration that does not require tickets or admission.
cards.source_title: Traditions - Rolling Toomer's Corner
cards.access_notes: Occurs after major athletic victories; the intersection is a public landmark.

cards.title: Study in the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: 231 Mell Street
cards.notes: Access the Learning Commons for group study or the quiet floors for individual work. Public visitors can read books on-site without a card.
cards.short_summary: The main university library featuring extensive study spaces, computer labs, and public access to collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Auburn University Libraries are open to the public for on-site use of materials and study spaces.
cards.source_title: Is the library open to the public? - LibAnswers
cards.access_notes: Open late during semesters; check official website for current daily hours.

cards.title: Visit the Red Barn
cards.subtitle: 620 South Donahue Drive
cards.notes: Walk the 30-acre park and view the iconic Red Barn. This scenic area serves as a tribute to Alabama's agricultural roots and is open for public strolls.
cards.short_summary: A scenic 30-acre park on campus featuring the historic Red Barn and open green space.
cards.evidence_claim: Ag Heritage Park is a gathering place for students and the community, serving as a scenic campus destination.
cards.source_title: Campus and Community | Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park areas are generally accessible; the Red Barn (ALFA Pavilion) is used for scheduled events.

cards.title: Attend Student Social Events
cards.subtitle: 910 South College Street
cards.notes: Look for 'Kickin' It at the Gogue' and other free student-only events. These programs often include line dancing and social mixers with no entry fee.
cards.short_summary: A performing arts venue that hosts specific free social events and programs for the student body.
cards.evidence_claim: Events like 'Kickin' It at the Gogue' are free and open to all Auburn University students.
cards.source_title: Kickin' It at the Gogue - AUinvolve
cards.access_notes: Free events typically require student ID and advance registration via AUinvolve.

cards.title: Study with a Stadium View
cards.subtitle: 405 West Magnolia Avenue
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor of Horton Hardgrave Hall to access this rooftop terrace. It offers collaborative seating and views of Jordan-Hare Stadium.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop terrace in the business building providing outdoor study space and campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: The rooftop Gavin Terrace of Horton Hardgrave Hall is a popular free study spot for students.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building operating hours; primarily intended for student use.

cards.title: Use the Indoor Track
cards.subtitle: 601 Heisman Drive
cards.notes: Walk or run on the 1/3-mile corkscrew track. Access is included in student fees, making it a 'no-extra-cost' hang for current students.
cards.short_summary: A premier fitness facility for students featuring a unique corkscrew track and leisure pool.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recreation and Wellness Center is available to Auburn students as part of their enrollment.
cards.source_title: Member Services | Auburn University Recreation and Wellness
cards.access_notes: Requires valid Tiger Card for entry; a one-time waiver must be signed on RWC Connect.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From high-tech engineering hubs to quiet library floors and scenic rooftop terraces, Auburn offers a diverse range of environments for focused academic work.

cards.title: Quiet Zone on the Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: RBD Library Quiet Study
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor for a strictly enforced quiet environment. It is the go-to spot for deep focus and individual work away from the collaborative buzz of the lower levels.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet study floor in the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth floor of the Ralph Brown Draughon Library is designated as an individual quiet study area.
cards.source_title: Are there any quiet study areas in the library? - LibAnswers
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; check library hours for late-night access during finals.

cards.title: Glass-Enclosed Group Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mell Classroom Building @ RBD
cards.notes: Reserve one of the 40 glass-enclosed study rooms via the online booking system. These spaces offer acoustic privacy and integrated technology for group projects.
cards.short_summary: Modern, reservable group study rooms with high-tech amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mell Classroom Building features 40 study rooms that can be reserved using the Skedda system.
cards.source_title: Mell Classroom Building | EASL - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via aub.ie/studyroombooking; check-in within 10 minutes.

cards.title: Gavin Terrace Rooftop
cards.subtitle: Harbert College of Business
cards.notes: Study with a view of Jordan-Hare Stadium from this fourth-floor rooftop terrace. It features covered seating and power outlets for outdoor productivity.
cards.short_summary: A scenic rooftop terrace offering outdoor study space for business students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gavin Terrace on the fourth floor of Horton-Hardgrave Hall offers collaborative working spaces and views of Jordan-Hare Stadium.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.

cards.title: Engineering Achievement Hub
cards.subtitle: Brown-Kopel Center
cards.notes: Utilize the spacious study areas on the top floor or the ground-floor maker spaces. This center is designed for collaboration across all engineering disciplines.
cards.short_summary: A comprehensive active-learning environment for engineering students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brown-Kopel Center includes ample student study areas, maker spaces, and laboratories across three stories.
cards.source_title: Brown-Kopel Engineering Student Achievement Center - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Check current semester hours for building access.

cards.entity_name: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
cards.title: Artistic Inspiration in the Lobby
cards.subtitle: Museum Study Space
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner among modular couches in the museum lobby. It is a peaceful alternative to the library, with free admission and an on-site café.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, art-filled study environment with modular seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lobby has modular couches for group sessions or relaxed reading, and admission is free.
cards.source_title: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art - College Students
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Sunday 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; extended hours until 8 p.m. on Thursdays.

cards.title: ACLC Relaxation Zones
cards.subtitle: Academic Classroom Complex
cards.notes: Located next to The Edge dining hall, this complex features adaptable classrooms and dedicated quiet study areas for students between labs.
cards.short_summary: Modern quiet study and relaxation areas within a major lab complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The ACLC features adaptable classroom spaces, labs, and quiet study areas.
cards.source_title: Auburn University opens new Academic Classroom and Laboratory Complex
cards.access_notes: Open during standard academic building hours.

cards.title: Student Center Quiet Lounges
cards.subtitle: Melton Student Center
cards.notes: The third floor offers quiet study areas and meeting spaces. It is a central campus hub with easy access to dining and student resources.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study lounges located on the upper floor of the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harold D. Melton Student Center offers meeting spaces and quiet study areas.
cards.source_title: Harold D. Melton Student Center - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check for specific holiday or break hours.

cards.entity_name: Tony and Libba Rane Culinary Science Center
cards.title: Woltosz Rooftop Terrace
cards.subtitle: Rane Culinary Science Center
cards.notes: Visit this rooftop garden before 3 p.m. for a quiet study session with views of Samford Hall. It features sun-soaked seating and shaded umbrellas.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop garden terrace open to students during daytime hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walt and Ginger Woltosz Rooftop Terrace is open to students until 3 p.m. each day.
cards.source_title: Find out where students are studying this fall - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Student access ends at 3 p.m. daily before transitioning to a commercial venue.

cards.title: Lowder Ground Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: Harbert College of Business
cards.notes: Located near the Starbucks on the ground floor, this area (Room 023) provides a convenient spot for business students to work between classes.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated student study area on the ground floor of the business building.
cards.evidence_claim: Lowder Hall Ground Floor features a student study area in room 023.
cards.source_title: Harbert College of Business Locations - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Primarily for students enrolled in Harbert College of Business classes.

cards.title: FWE Student Organization Lounge
cards.subtitle: College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment
cards.notes: The second floor houses a student lounge and organization space (Room 2207). It offers a quiet, specialized environment for natural resource majors.
cards.short_summary: A specialized student lounge and study area for FWE majors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forestry and Wildlife Sciences Building includes a student organization and lounge area on the second floor.
cards.source_title: FWE Building Room Directory - College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment
cards.access_notes: Access may be restricted to students within the College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Auburn University, from the historic Toomer's Corner to the bustling student housing districts.

cards.title: The Gateway to Downtown
cards.subtitle: Intersection of Magnolia Avenue and College Street
cards.notes: Visit the historic intersection where campus meets the city to celebrate major athletic victories by rolling the iconic oak trees with toilet paper.
cards.short_summary: The historic intersection of Magnolia Avenue and College Street serving as the primary gathering spot for Auburn victory celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Toomer's Corner is a street corner located at the intersection of Magnolia Avenue and College Street, marking the northeastern-most reach of the campus and the beginning of downtown.
cards.source_title: A brief history of Rolling Toomer's Corner & Toomer's Drugstore - Auburn-Opelika Tourism
cards.access_notes: Public intersection accessible 24/7; Toomer's Drugs typically closes by 6:00 PM or 7:00 PM.

cards.title: The Student Living Corridor
cards.subtitle: West Magnolia Avenue
cards.notes: Walk this major thoroughfare to find high-density student housing complexes and popular local eateries like Momma Goldberg's Deli.
cards.short_summary: A primary east-west corridor lined with modern student apartment complexes and long-standing local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: West Magnolia Avenue is home to several major student housing developments including 320 West Mag and The Magnolia at Auburn.
cards.source_title: Location | Student Apartments Near Auburn University | The Mill
cards.access_notes: Public street with various business hours; generally active late into the evening due to student housing.

cards.title: The Downtown Retail Hub
cards.subtitle: North College Street
cards.notes: Browse local boutiques and bookstores along this central downtown block, which serves as a primary shopping destination for students.
cards.short_summary: The main north-south commercial artery of downtown Auburn, featuring a high concentration of retail shops and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: North College Street features prominent local businesses such as Toomer's Drugs and J&M Bookstore, serving as a hub for student retail.
cards.source_title: Retail — Downtown Auburn
cards.access_notes: Public sidewalk access 24/7; most retail shops open 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

cards.title: The Parkside Connection
cards.subtitle: South Gay Street
cards.notes: Follow this street south from downtown to reach Town Creek Park, a popular off-campus green space for walking and relaxation.
cards.short_summary: A street connecting the downtown core to residential areas and significant municipal parks used by the student population.
cards.evidence_claim: Town Creek Park is located at 1150 South Gay Street and is described as a go-to spot for students needing to clear their mind.
cards.source_title: 7 places every college student loves in Auburn | The Bama Buzz
cards.access_notes: Public street; Town Creek Park is open from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: The Modern Residential Block
cards.subtitle: West Glenn Avenue
cards.notes: Observe the rapid development of luxury student housing like UNCOMMON Auburn along this busy northern edge of downtown.
cards.short_summary: A major thoroughfare north of campus that has become a focal point for new multi-story student apartment developments.
cards.evidence_claim: West Glenn Avenue is the site of several new student housing projects, including UNCOMMON Auburn at 250 W Glenn Ave.
cards.source_title: Neighborhood | UNCOMMON Auburn
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require keycard access for entry.

cards.title: The Campus-Adjacent Link
cards.subtitle: Wright Street
cards.notes: Walk this short connector street between Glenn and Magnolia to access several new student housing complexes within steps of the campus core.
cards.short_summary: A north-south street located directly adjacent to the university's northeastern boundary, undergoing significant residential redevelopment.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmark Properties purchased a site on Wright Street between West Glenn and Magnolia avenues for a new student housing community.
cards.source_title: New 825-bed student housing apartment coming to downtown Auburn | The Bama Buzz
cards.access_notes: Public street; heavily used by pedestrians walking to the Harbert College of Business.

cards.title: The Downtown Dining Row
cards.subtitle: East Magnolia Avenue
cards.notes: Explore a variety of local restaurants and cafes, such as Hamilton's on Magnolia, located just east of the Toomer's Corner intersection.
cards.short_summary: The eastern portion of Magnolia Avenue featuring a mix of upscale and casual dining options popular with students and visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: East Magnolia Avenue hosts several local hotspots including Hamilton's on Magnolia at 174 E Magnolia Ave.
cards.source_title: Location | Student Apartments Near Auburn University | The Mill
cards.access_notes: Public street; restaurant hours vary, with many serving lunch and dinner daily.

cards.title: The Southern Commercial Strip
cards.subtitle: South College Street
cards.notes: Visit this busy corridor for essential student services, including the Alumni Hall retail store and various fast-casual dining options.
cards.short_summary: A major north-south thoroughfare south of Toomer's Corner that provides critical commercial services to the university community.
cards.evidence_claim: South College Street is lined with local eateries and shops, including Alumni Hall at 339 South College Street.
cards.source_title: How to Find Off-Campus Housing Near Auburn University - Apartments.com
cards.access_notes: Public street; retail hours typically 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM.

cards.title: The Urban Living District
cards.subtitle: North Gay Street
cards.notes: Find high-rise student living options like The Standard at Auburn, located just a few blocks north of the downtown commercial center.
cards.short_summary: A street north of the downtown core that has seen significant development of mid-rise student apartment buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Standard at Auburn is located at 234 N Gay St, providing upscale student living near the heart of campus.
cards.source_title: The Standard at Auburn: Auburn Off Campus Housing
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential complexes are private with secure entry.

cards.title: The Residential Transition
cards.subtitle: East Samford Avenue
cards.notes: Travel east along this avenue to see the transition from campus-adjacent housing to established residential neighborhoods and local schools.
cards.short_summary: An east-west street that connects the southern edge of the downtown area to residential districts and community facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: East Samford Avenue is home to community landmarks like the East Samford School and various apartment complexes.
cards.source_title: East Samford School - Home
cards.access_notes: Public street; primarily residential and school zone.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and superstitions that define the Auburn Family, from rolling the oaks to the pre-game eagle flight.

cards.title: Rolling Toomer's Corner
cards.subtitle: A Snowy Celebration of Victory
cards.notes: Toss rolls of toilet paper into the oak trees at the intersection of College and Magnolia after every major Auburn win.
cards.short_summary: Auburn fans celebrate athletic victories by covering the iconic Toomer's Oaks in toilet paper, a tradition dating back to the 1960s.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition of rolling Toomer's Corner began in the 1960s when employees at Toomer's Drugs threw telegraph ticker tape into the trees to signal away-game wins.
cards.source_title: Traditions - Rolling Toomer's Corner - Auburn Tigers
cards.access_notes: Open to the public after victories; participants should bring their own rolls of toilet paper.

cards.title: The Tiger Walk
cards.subtitle: The Original Gameday Procession
cards.notes: Line Donahue Drive two hours before kickoff to high-five players and coaches as they walk from the Athletics Complex to the stadium.
cards.short_summary: Thousands of fans line the street to cheer the football team into Jordan-Hare Stadium, a tradition that began in the 1960s.
cards.evidence_claim: Tiger Walk began in the 1960s when kids would walk up the street to meet the team for autographs; it now draws over 20,000 fans for major games.
cards.source_title: Traditions - Tiger Walk - Auburn Tigers
cards.access_notes: Occurs two hours before every home game along South Donahue Drive.

cards.title: The War Eagle Flight
cards.subtitle: A Majestic Pre-Game Ritual
cards.notes: Watch a golden or bald eagle circle the stadium and land at midfield as the crowd chants 'War Eagle' before kickoff.
cards.short_summary: A live eagle from the Southeastern Raptor Center performs a free flight over the crowd before home football games.
cards.evidence_claim: The eagle flight is a unique Auburn tradition where a raptor circles the entire stadium before landing, symbolizing the school's battle cry.
cards.source_title: See War Eagle | Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Visible to ticket holders inside Jordan-Hare Stadium before home games.

cards.title: Hey Day
cards.subtitle: The Friendliest Day on the Plains
cards.notes: Wear a provided nametag and greet everyone you pass with a friendly 'Hey' to promote campus unity.
cards.short_summary: An annual tradition since 1947 where students and faculty wear nametags to foster a welcoming environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Hey Day was established in 1947 to help World War II veterans transition back to campus and feel recognized by the student body.
cards.source_title: Auburn Tradition: The History of Hey Day
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall; nametags are distributed at various campus locations.

cards.title: Cater Callouts
cards.subtitle: Public Membership Announcements
cards.notes: Gather at the back steps of Cater Hall to hear the names of new members selected for major campus organizations.
cards.short_summary: A student-led tradition where organizations announce their new rosters from the steps of the historic Katherine Cooper Cater Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Callouts are a sacred tradition unique to Auburn students where groups like the cheerleading team and SGA announce new members publicly.
cards.source_title: Cater Callouts - On The Lawn
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the evenings following organization tryouts or elections.

cards.title: The Seal Superstition
cards.subtitle: Don't Step on the Curse
cards.notes: Avoid stepping on the university seal embedded in the sidewalk in front of Langdon Hall to ensure you graduate on time.
cards.short_summary: A campus legend warns that stepping on the seal will prevent graduation in four years and curse your future family.
cards.evidence_claim: Legend says stepping on the seal means you won't graduate in four years, won't find true love, and will have seven generations of Alabama fans.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions – Don't Step On the Seal!
cards.access_notes: The seal is located on the ground at the front entrance of Langdon Hall.

cards.title: The Auburn Creed
cards.subtitle: The Moral Compass of the Plains
cards.notes: Memorize and live by the ten stanzas written by George Petrie in 1943, which define the spirit of the Auburn Family.
cards.short_summary: A foundational document outlining the values of hard work, honesty, and helpfulness that all Auburn students strive to embody.
cards.evidence_claim: Written in 1943 by George Petrie, the Creed is a unifying set of beliefs common to all Auburn students, faculty, and alumni.
cards.source_title: The Auburn Creed | Auburn University
cards.access_notes: The Creed is displayed in various campus buildings and celebrated annually on Creed Day.

cards.title: The Bodda Getta Chant
cards.subtitle: Nonsensical Spirit
cards.notes: Join the student section in reciting this rhythmic, fast-paced cheer that ends with a thunderous 'Auburn Tigers, Rah! Rah! Rah!'
cards.short_summary: Auburn's most famous nonsensical cheer, performed at athletic events to energize the crowd.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bodda Getta chant was made an official cheer in the 1960s and is a favorite tradition in the student section.
cards.source_title: Get Your Hands Up for Bodda Getta!
cards.access_notes: Performed at most home athletic events, particularly football and basketball.

cards.title: Wreck Tech Pajama Parade
cards.subtitle: A Bygone Rivalry Ritual
cards.notes: Learn about the historic parade where students marched in pajamas to 'grease the tracks' before the Georgia Tech game.
cards.short_summary: A discontinued but legendary tradition where students wore pajamas to a pep rally and parade before playing Georgia Tech.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wreck Tech Parade began in the early 1930s and was a staple of the Auburn-Georgia Tech rivalry until 1987.
cards.source_title: Incredible footage from the 1983 Auburn Wreck Tech parade
cards.access_notes: This tradition is currently inactive but remains a significant part of university history.

cards.title: Ring Night & Curse Reversal
cards.subtitle: Cleansing the Class Ring
cards.notes: Dip your official class ring in the President's fountain to 'cleanse' it after tapping it on the cursed seal.
cards.short_summary: A modern tradition for juniors and seniors to celebrate receiving their official Auburn rings.
cards.evidence_claim: Part of the Ring Tradition involves 'cursing' the ring by tapping it on the Seal and 'cleansing' it in the President's fountain.
cards.source_title: Traditions - Auburn University Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Held annually for students who have purchased the official Auburn ring.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Auburn University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Friday: Walk the Concourse
cards.subtitle: The heart of campus activity
cards.notes: Walk this central pedestrian path to see student organizations tabling and get a feel for the campus energy on your first Friday.
cards.short_summary: A bustling central pedestrian thoroughfare where student groups gather to share information and host events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Haley Concourse is located in the center of campus and is constantly buzzing with activity, making it an ideal setting for students to learn about organizations.
cards.source_title: Haley Concourse - Auburn University Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public outdoor walkway; most active during weekday class hours.

cards.title: Friday: Dinner at The Edge
cards.subtitle: Campus culinary hub
cards.notes: Grab dinner at this two-story dining hall featuring diverse food stations and plenty of seating for meeting new classmates.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant, two-story dining facility serving as the primary culinary hub for the Auburn student community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Edge at Central Dining serves more than 5,000 students daily and features diverse stations in a vibrant two-story space.
cards.source_title: The Edge at Central Dining - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students with meal plans; guest entry available for purchase.

cards.title: Friday: Evening at the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Late-night student hangout
cards.notes: Head to the student center for evening events or to relax in the lounges; it stays open late for student use.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, housing dining options, meeting rooms, and student organization offices.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harold D. Melton Student Center is open from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Harold D. Melton Student Center - Auburn University Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Saturday: Morning Workout
cards.subtitle: State-of-the-art fitness
cards.notes: Start your Saturday with a run on the 1/3-mile corkscrew track or visit the leisure pool at this massive recreation facility.
cards.short_summary: A 240,000 square foot facility featuring a unique corkscrew track, climbing towers, and a leisure pool.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recreation and Wellness Center features a 1/3-mile corkscrew track and is available for use by any Auburn student.
cards.source_title: Member Services | Auburn University Recreation and Wellness
cards.access_notes: Full access included for enrolled students via Auburn ID or the AuburnRec app.

cards.title: Saturday: Stadium Tour
cards.subtitle: Home of the Tigers
cards.notes: Take a guided tour to see the locker rooms and press box of one of college football's most iconic venues.
cards.short_summary: The 88,043-seat home stadium for Auburn Tigers football, offering behind-the-scenes tours on non-gamedays.
cards.evidence_claim: Daily stadium tours provide a behind-the-scenes look at the Harbert Recruiting Center, Gameday Locker Room, and Press Box.
cards.source_title: VIP Daily Tours - Auburn Tigers
cards.access_notes: Tours are approximately one hour; registration is required and typically held on non-gamedays.

cards.title: Saturday: Lemonade at Toomer's
cards.subtitle: A historic Auburn tradition
cards.notes: Visit the intersection of campus and downtown for a world-famous lemonade at Toomer's Drugs, an Auburn landmark since 1896.
cards.short_summary: The historic intersection where campus meets downtown, famous for its lemonade and victory celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Toomer's Drugs has been an Auburn landmark since 1896 and is famous for its lemonade at the corner of Magnolia and College.
cards.source_title: Directions - Toomer's Drugs
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 10:00 AM - 5:30 PM, Saturday 10:00 AM - 7:00 PM, Sunday 12:00 PM - 5:00 PM.

cards.entity_name: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
cards.title: Sunday: Explore the Galleries
cards.subtitle: Cultural heart of campus
cards.notes: Spend a quiet Sunday afternoon exploring 19th and 20th-century American and European art in these free galleries.
cards.short_summary: Auburn's accredited art museum featuring a permanent collection and rotating exhibitions with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is open Tuesday through Sunday from 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and admission is free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: College Students - Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
cards.access_notes: Open Sunday 10:00 AM - 4:30 PM; closed on Mondays.

cards.title: Sunday: Nature Walk
cards.subtitle: 16-acre botanic garden
cards.notes: Walk the shaded trails and see native Alabama plants in this peaceful outdoor classroom located right on campus.
cards.short_summary: A 16-acre facility dedicated to the display and conservation of native woody plants of the Southeastern United States.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum is open every day of the year from sunrise to sunset with no charge for admission.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Donald E. Davis Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset.

cards.title: Sunday: Relax at Samford
cards.subtitle: Iconic campus green space
cards.notes: Join other students on the lawn in front of Samford Hall to play frisbee or relax under the trees before classes start.
cards.short_summary: The iconic green space in front of Samford Hall, serving as a primary gathering spot for the Auburn community.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford Park is located directly in front of Samford Hall and is a favorite spot in the Auburn community for outdoor activities.
cards.source_title: Samford Hall - Auburn University Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public outdoor park.

cards.title: Sunday: Prep for Monday
cards.subtitle: Modern study spaces
cards.notes: Find a study nook or a 'spark*space' in this modern building to organize your notes and prepare for your first full week of classes.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art active learning facility connected to the main library, featuring numerous informal study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mell Classroom Building features 40 study spaces and informal learning areas designed for student collaboration.
cards.source_title: Mell Classroom Building | EASL - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Connected to the RBD Library; hours typically match library operating times.
